beats.name: hook
beats.said: A man stakes everything he owns on the race's weakest runner.
beats.shown: Mint-vest man with a mallet beside a pink piggy bank on a track-side table; bank bursts at 1.0 s; camera whips to horses in dust and a plodding white horse with a jockey.

beats.name: setup
beats.said: The room laughs at his idle day; a friend watches from the hilltop with a giant mirror.
beats.shown: Betting room with odds board and jeering regulars; protagonist smug on a window bench; mirror dive to the town street; buddy with a gold-framed mirror on a meadow hill.

beats.name: escalation
beats.said: Favorites keep winning and the hilltop stays unlit; the regulars tease him; the final race is a rout.
beats.shown: Circular mirror view of the grandstand cutting back and forth with the buddy on the hill; regulars at a barrel; bench banter; grandstand race; empty track to a parking lot.

beats.name: twist
beats.said: A flash from the hill; he stakes everything on horse nine; the clerk mocks its record.
beats.shown: Window sun flash; protagonist carries a green cash bundle to the cage; dim red-walled teller close-up (bill on forehead, laughing); dairy cart on the finish street.

beats.name: explainer
beats.said: Back then, results came into betting rooms by telegraph wire, so wagers stayed open until it clicked.
beats.shown: Striped stands and target pole, judges' booth, fast fly-through of a dusk street with a spark on the wire into a telegraph nook with an odds chalkboard; regulars at the barrel.

beats.name: payoff
beats.said: From the hill, the buddy watches horse nine surge out of nowhere and win by a nose.
beats.shown: Sunset hill, buddy peering through a huge brass lens; camera dives through it into the track; white horse 9 overtakes in orange light with dust and motion blur.

beats.name: ending
beats.said: While the room still laughs, the wire clicks out the winner; once it spells nine, the laughter dies.
beats.shown: Dusk betting room: odds board, ladder man, crowd; sign letters N-I-N-E appear one by one; banknotes rain on the group; heckler's grin turns to shock; final still hold.

hook.first_frame: Protagonist (round white head, small hat, mint vest, polka-dot bow tie) stands behind a wooden table at the track with a mallet raised, a pink piggy bank beside him; white rail and blue sky behind; no caption yet.
hook.first_3s: 0-1.0 s mallet raised, he smirks and blinks, slow push-in; about 1.0 s piggy bank bursts into shards and coins, camera whips away; 1.6-3.0 s low rail view of horses in dust, then a slow white horse with a jockey.
hook.title_vs_first_line: Title names the gimmick (a mirror rigging a race); the first line gives only the odd bet on the slowest horse, so the mirror is withheld until about 9.5 s.

story.structure: act first, explain at the end
story.real_fact_core: Race results reached betting rooms by telegraph wire with a delay and bets stayed open until it arrived, so a faster signal (a mirror flash from the hill) lets someone bet on a race already decided.
story.protagonist: Silent, smug bettor in a boater hat, mint vest and polka-dot bow tie (the 'mirror man')
story.authority_or_antagonist: Mocking regulars (plaid-vest man in a derby, round-glasses man) and a pitying teller; no true villain

tone.humour: Absurd exaggeration (a jockey waving at his mother, a horse so far back it is in the car park, a nag beaten by the dairy wagon it hauls) plus small visual gags (pretzel, bill on the teller's head).
tone.deadpan_or_irony: Deadpan narration with dramatic irony: the audience knows the dark hill matters while the room mocks him; the ending flips the room from laughing to stunned.
tone.dialogue_style: Short taunts and one-liners from side characters plus a viewer-voiced question; faces and mouths animate while lines are spoken; no speech bubbles.

character_style.outline: Thick dark-navy ink line, near-constant width, about 0.7-1.5% of frame width depending on shot scale; it grows with a push-in, so it is part of the artwork, not a screen-space filter (estimate).
character_style.shading: Mostly flat fills with a soft lavender-grey gradient on the shaded side of heads and a darker band low on the vest; faint warm rim in sunset scenes (estimate).
character_style.consistency_between_shots: Very high: identical shapes, colours and line weight in every shot; heads stay frontal or side-on with features shifting to show a turn (estimate); background regulars reuse the same head and limb kit.

animation.body_motion: 2D stick-limb puppets: held poses with swaps of arm and leg positions, slight head tilts, arm raises for props (mallet, mirror, pretzel). Big movement comes from the camera and 3D FX, not the characters.
animation.eyes_and_blinks: Eyes are black dots or ovals that swap between half-lid, open, wide rings and closed lines; a closed-eye frame at f12 looks like a blink; none caught in the sampled frames of the 8.5-10 s hold (estimate).
animation.idle_motion: Every 0.3-0.5 s the head tilts a few degrees or the face swaps (the smirk lands as 'smiling' is said, f275); legs sway slightly; torso otherwise still; the set is static apart from the camera push-in.
animation.squash_and_stretch: None seen on characters; teller's head may pulse slightly on the laugh at f1256-1262 (could be the camera push-in); stretch appears only in FX (shards, tumbling bills).

generation_evidence.observation: Piggy bank bursts into glossy shards, coins and dust that fly with consistent shading and lighting; pieces keep rigid shape from frame to frame.
Camera dives through a hand mirror: foreground heads scale up with parallax, background blurs with real depth of field, outlines grow with the object, geometry stays solid.
In-world sign letters N-I-N-E appear crisply one by one and stay readable; banknotes tumble and pile up without morphing; the MILK RUN 1000-1 plate stays identical.
Teller's face redraws as discrete mouth shapes (D, closed, round O) with identical outline, visor and banknote in all frames; no limb or texture drift.
Fast fly-through from the street into the telegraph nook keeps perspective, signs (BETS OPEN, horse-name board) and room geometry consistent frame to frame: a built set.
The same odds board with the 9 MILK RUN plate and the same characters recur identically across the video with matching text and colours: reused assets, not regenerated images.
